description:
Fold V-9 + V-11 — two findings of the 2026-09-03 re-run of count (ii), both on §7.1, both additive, both KCB-only. One edit.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored).

V-9 — `payload_schema_id` IS NOT CONSUMER-VERIFIABLE. §7.1 states a canonicalization for `schema_id` in five numbered steps (keep only shape keys; normalize values; normalize the serialization; hash and prefix; name the rule) and states NONE for `payload_schema_id`. The 0.5.0 fold made `payload_schema_id` a shape key kept INSIDE that canonicalization, and described it as a digest 'over its own canonical declaration of that payload' — but no verb retrieves that declaration. §4's five verbs are `discover`, `describe`, `invoke`, `subscribe`, `fetch`; `describe` fetches the AgentCard plus `tools/list` tool schemas, and `fetch` is a CAS GET by `asset` id. So a consumer told by §2.1 that a payload cross-check EXISTS cannot perform it: it holds a digest, and nothing hands it the bytes the digest is over. §7.1's *falsifiability is the point* paragraph — 'a consumer recomputes the digest from the card it fetched itself and compares it against the published value' — is true of `schema_id` and false of `payload_schema_id`.

V-11 — THE RULE ID IS `MAY` ON THE BRANCH THAT NEEDS A `MUST`. §7.1 step 5 reads: 'A `schema_id` MAY carry a canonicalization rule id in its prefix, as `sha256/<rule>-<lowercase hex>`. An absent rule id means `kcb1`.' The MUST NOT lands on the branch that does not need it — 'a provider MUST NOT emit a `kcb2` prefix for such a port', where 'such a port' is one declaring NO `payload_schema_id` and therefore canonicalizing byte-identically under both rules. There is no MUST on the branch that does: a port that DOES declare a `payload_schema_id` digests differently under `kcb2` than under `kcb1`, and may publish that digest under the absent prefix, which step 5 defines to mean `kcb1`. A consumer then compares two digests computed under two rules while believing them comparable — restoring exactly the non-recoverable *silent mutation* verdict V-3's fold was written to prevent.

THE FOLD. Additive, KCB-only, one §7.1 edit: state a canonicalization for `payload_schema_id` and a way for a consumer to obtain the declaration it digests (or, if the honest answer is that the cross-check cannot be made verifiable without a verb KCB does not have, say THAT normatively and make §2.1/§7.1 read consistently with it rather than promising a check that cannot be performed); and turn step 5's rule id into a MUST on the branch whose digest depends on it, leaving the absent prefix meaning `kcb1` so NO PUBLISHED DIGEST MOVES.

THEN RE-RUN COUNT (ii). Expect it NOT to close on this tasklist alone: V-10 is the third finding of the same re-run and lands in `950`. Record the verdict honestly rather than implying the count moved.

userStories.title: V-9 — a payload cross-check a consumer can actually perform, or an honest statement that it cannot
userStories.description: §7.1 promises a cross-check and gives a consumer no way to run it. Close the gap, or state the limit normatively — but do not leave a clause that reads as a check and is not one.
acceptanceCriteria: §7.1 states a canonicalization for `payload_schema_id` with the same determinism its five `schema_id` steps have, so two providers declaring the same payload produce the same digest and one provider re-serializing produces no drift.

The declaration the digest is over is OBTAINABLE by the consumer that is told a cross-check exists — verified against §4's five verbs rather than assumed (`describe` fetches the card plus `tools/list` tool schemas; `fetch` is a CAS GET by `asset` id). If the honest conclusion is that no existing verb carries it, the fold says so NORMATIVELY and makes §2.1 and §7.1 read consistently with that limit instead of promising a check nothing can perform; adding a sixth verb is out of scope for this fold and any such finding is recorded rather than built.

§7.1's *falsifiability is the point* paragraph is made true of both digests, or is scoped to the one it is true of. A reader must not be able to come away believing `payload_schema_id` is recomputable when it is not.
Additive and KCB-only: no verb is added, no plane or port kind is added, `payload_schema_id` stays OPTIONAL, and a card conformant at 0.5.0 stays conformant. Checked against the text.

GATES: `node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs`, `node scripts/check-registry.mjs`, `node scripts/check-tasklist-categories.mjs` and `bash scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh` all green, with the observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: KCB 0.5.3: §7.1 gains NORMATIVE (a)-(e) for `payload_schema_id` + a scoped falsifiability paragraph; §2.1 pointer extended. (a) sha256 over the declaration's published bytes (a content address, KINP §3 `asset` form), no key set so step 5's rule id MUST NOT appear; (b) determinism yes, cross-provider convergence explicitly NOT claimed; (c) §4's five verbs checked one by one — `fetch` is the only carrier, because the digest already IS an `asset` address; (d) two branches, retrievable = fact, unretrievable = provider-attested with failure mode 2 declared open; (e) no provider obligation added. Sixth verb + reserved capability name refused on the record with a re-open condition. Additive: operand stays OPTIONAL, no verb/field/plane/port kind added, §7.2 table undisturbed, step 1 kept set and kcb1/kcb2 byte-unchanged so no published digest moves. GATES all green: check-doc-integrity exit 0 ('OK — every relative link resolves and all 3 status tables match their headers', 61 md files / 1782 links, capability-bus 0.5.3 candidate); check-doc-links --ratchet --base main '0 dead vs 1 on main, retired 1'; check-schemas 'OK' (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures); check-registry 'OK' (31 relation names); check-tasklist-categories 'OK — 6 tasklists categorized'; check-roadmap-truth exit 0 (coverage/stale/park all OK). Also fixed a pre-existing dead link in promotability.md:54 (930 tasklist moved to tasks/chief/completed/) which had doc-integrity red on main.

userStories.title: V-11 — the rule id becomes a MUST on the branch whose digest depends on it
userStories.description: Step 5's MAY sits on the branch that needs a MUST, and its MUST NOT sits on the branch that does not. Swap the strengths without moving a published digest.
acceptanceCriteria: §7.1 step 5 requires (MUST) a canonicalization rule id on a digest whose value DEPENDS on the rule — a knowledge port declaring a `payload_schema_id`, which digests differently under `kcb2` than under `kcb1`.

The absent prefix still means `kcb1` and NO PUBLISHED DIGEST MOVES. The existing MUST NOT on emitting a `kcb2` prefix for a port that canonicalizes byte-identically under both rules is preserved, so the two branches now carry opposite, correct strengths.

The consumer-side rules are unchanged and re-checked: an unknown rule id is read as *no cross-check available*, never as a defect and never as a mutation (§7.2); comparison is meaningful only between digests computed under the same rule id; growing §2.1's shape vocabulary again mints the NEXT rule id.

V-3's verdict is restored in the text rather than in a comment: the case §7.2 makes non-recoverable is reserved for the same rule, the same port, a moved digest and an unmoved version — and a `kcb2` digest published under the absent prefix can no longer reach it.

The KCB version move is decided under §7.2's own table and recorded with reasoning; if it moves, all three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it, and §2.3's legacy namespace-root removal declared at KCB 0.6.0 is checked rather than tripped.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: KCB 0.5.3 (same publication as US-1, extended not re-bumped): §7.1 step 5 gains a third bullet, the MIRROR of the existing MUST NOT — a provider MUST emit the rule id of the rule it actually canonicalized under, EXCEPT where that canonicalization is byte-identical to `kcb1`'s for the port in hand. Both arms stated by PROPERTY, neither names a rule, so they carry to the next rule id unchanged. Bullet 1's MAY dropped and the absent prefix declared a STATEMENT, not a silence (why it is a MUST not a SHOULD). Correction path stated: re-publishing a mislabelled digest with its true rule id moves the prefix and not the hex, reads *incomparable*, so re-discovery is the recovery — and a provider MUST NOT leave a mislabel standing on the ground that correcting it would move a value. §7.2's *not a silent mutation* bullet now records that its own reservation (same rule, same port, moved digest, unmoved version) HOLDS BECAUSE of this MUST — V-3's verdict restored in the text. §2.1 pointer extended. Consumer-side rules re-checked and unchanged (unknown rule id = *no cross-check available*; comparison only within one rule id; growing §2.1's vocabulary mints the next rule id). NO PUBLISHED DIGEST MOVES — every digest published to date is `kcb1` and stays prefix-free, both key sets byte-unchanged, no next rule id minted, `sha256/<rule>-<hex>` form is 0.5.0's; §2's worked AgentCard needed NO correction (checked: its one port declaring a `payload_schema_id` already carries `sha256/kcb2-…`, every port declaring none carries a bare `sha256-…`). VERSION DECIDED: stays PATCH at 0.5.3. §7.2's table governs *a published capability* and has no row for a spec-axis bump (declaring one under it is BP-8/AP-9's defect, not repeated); it IS consulted for the two questions it answers — does a published digest move (no), does a live subscriber break (no) — and its ROWS ARE UNDISTURBED. The narrowing is stated rather than hidden: strictly a provider reading 0.5.2 permissively could publish a `kcb2` digest bare and now cannot, but the set narrowed is one 0.5.2's own text does not determine (the break-test's finding was that it enforces NEITHER reading), so the stricter reading DISAMBIGUATES. §2.3's 0.6.0 legacy-root removal CHECKED, NOT TRIPPED — no minor taken, so 0.6.0 stays spoken for. Version unmoved so the three status mirrors (README.md, specs/README.md, ECOSYSTEM.md) needed no edit — confirmed by doc-integrity's table diff. GATES all green: check-doc-integrity exit 0 ('OK — every relative link resolves and all 3 status tables match their headers'); check-doc-links --ratchet --base main exit 0 ('0 dead vs 1 on main, retired 1'); check-schemas exit 0 ('OK', 9 schemas / 278 positions / 80 $refs / 3 fixtures); check-registry exit 0 ('OK', 31 relation names); check-tasklist-categories exit 0 ('OK — 6 tasklists categorized'); check-roadmap-truth exit 0 (coverage/stale/park all OK). `chief verify` exit 0 RECORDED, tree dd3adb6e.

userStories.title: Re-run count (ii), and record honestly that V-10 still stands
userStories.description: The re-run is what the fold exists for. It is not expected to close the count — V-10 gates (ii) too and lands in `950`.
acceptanceCriteria: `scenarios/e2e-live-schema-mutation.md` is re-run BY HAND against the folded text for the steps V-9 and V-11 were found on, with a per-step verdict recorded in the scenario's re-run section.

The walk is against the PROSE: DR-7 records `kcs:live-schema-mutation` returning `green` over four blocking deltas, and the encoding still predates the 0.5.0 fold, so its exit code is not evidence about this one either.

The verdict is recorded honestly and the record states that count (ii) does NOT close while V-10 stands. Fold dispositions for V-9 and V-11 are added to the capability-versioning fold-disposition reference, each reasoning the fold's extent.
`docs/reference/promotability.md` is updated to match what this walk changed, and states that KCB's other counts are untouched by it.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
